description: General PATIENTS: for intensive therapy, including high dependency care
General PATIENTS: for normal therapy: where resources permit the admission of PATIENTS who might need all but intensive or high dependency therapy

General PATIENTS: for limited therapy: where nursing care rather than continuous medical care is provided. Such WARDS can be used only for PATIENTS carefully selected and restricted to a narrow range in terms of the extent and nature of disease
Younger physically disabled PATIENTS: spinal units, only those units which are nationally recognised
Younger physically disabled PATIENTS: other units
Neonates: not associated with the maternity WARD and in which there are some designated cots for intensive care
Neonates: non-maternity: not associated with the maternity WARD and without designated cots for intensive care
Neonates: maternity: associated with the maternity WARD in that cots are in the maternity WARD nursery or in the WARD itself
Only for maternity PATIENTS looked after by CONSULTANTS
Joint use for maternity PATIENTS looked after by CONSULTANTS and GENERAL MEDICAL PRACTITIONERS
Only for maternity PATIENTS looked after by GENERAL MEDICAL PRACTITIONERS

Mental Illness intensive care: specially designated ward for PATIENTS needing containment and more intensive management (e.g. Psychiatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU)). This is not to be confused with intensive nursing where PATIENTS may require one to one nursing while on a standard WARD
Mental Illness short stay: PATIENTS intended to stay less than a year
Mental Illness long stay: PATIENTS intended to stay a year or more
Learning Disability PATIENTS in a designated or interim secure unit
Learning Disability PATIENTS intending to stay less than a year
Learning Disability PATIENTS intending to stay a year or more
